analysis.title: GS Housing Market Activity Scale: Week of November 1: Scale Down 2% Sequentially as Key Indicators Decline Despite Modest Relief in Rates
key_insights: The GS Housing Activity Scale for the week of November 1 fell 2% sequentially and 13% YOY, leaving it 34% below the long-term average. The weekly scale reads 3 and the monthly scale reads 4 for September.

The sequential decline was led by home sales down 4%, purchase applications down 2% and a weaker median listing price. A 2% drop in active listings and a higher median new listing price partly offset these.
The 30-year mortgage rate fell 6bps to 7.18% per Freddie Mac, but is up 96bps YOY.
GS channel checks suggest housing activity has stayed weak into November.
Given the weak setup, GS is focused on builders with company-specific initiatives, including potential capital allocation, and highlights Buy-rated IBP.
If conditions improve, GS sees the most upside in MTH and DHI because of their entry-level exposure and a disciplined approach to balancing margins and uses of cash.

Indicators still holding up: median sale price flat YOY, active listings 4% below the 2019 average, sale-to-list ratio of 98.3% (37bps above the same week in 2019), time on market similar to 2019, and 27% of homes off market within 2 weeks vs 25% in 2019.
Indicators showing weakness: purchase applications down 20% YOY and 15% below the September average, median list price down 2% YOY, and home sales down 9% YOY.
Total mortgage applications fell 42% YOY and refinancings fell 60% YOY. ARMs were 11% of volume vs 9% a year ago.
GS expects near-term activity to remain under pressure from rates and the macro backdrop, and attributes the weakness to affordability concerns and buyer hesitancy.

market_movers.rationale: GS highlights IBP as a name with company-specific initiatives, including potential capital allocation, in a weak housing market. Rating and price of $199.12 are from the disclosures.
GS sees the greatest upside to MTH if builder conditions improve, given entry-level exposure and a disciplined approach to margins and cash use. Price of $64.19 is from the disclosures.
GS sees the greatest upside to DHI if builder conditions improve, given entry-level exposure and a disciplined approach to margins and cash use. Price of $147.48 is from the disclosures.

sector_views.rationale: Activity is weak and near-term pressure is expected. GS favors names with company-specific initiatives and sees upside in entry-level exposed builders only if conditions improve.

tension_points.bull_case: Several indicators hold up: median sale price flat YOY, sale-to-list ratio 37bps above 2019, and 27% of homes off market within 2 weeks vs 25% in 2019. GS sees potential for greater activity if headwinds abate.
tension_points.bear_case: Purchase applications are down 20% YOY, home sales down 9% YOY, and the 30-year rate is 7.18%. GS channel checks show weak activity into November and it expects near-term pressure.
tension_points.what_invalidates: GS does not name a specific level. It says activity could improve if affordability and economic headwinds abate.
